1.title: Responding in Defender XDR (1): Office 365, Purview, Cloud and Cloud Apps
1.text: Welcome to Module eleven: Responding in Defender X D R (one): Office three sixty-five, Purview, Cloud and Cloud Apps. It covers the exam area two. Respond to security incidents. Each part of this module comes from the study notes of the same name, so you can read the notes after you watch.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do five things. Investigate and remediate threats by using Microsoft Defender for Office three sixty-five, including automatic attack disruption. Investigate and remediate threats or compromised entities identified by Microsoft Purview. Investigate and remediate alerts and incidents identified by Microsoft Defender for Cloud workload protections. Investigate and remediate security risks identified by Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps. Practice with exam-style questions and a recall check.

1.title: Where This Fits in the Exam
1.text: Here is where this module sits in the exam. Exam area: two. Respond to security incidents (thirty-five to forty percent). Exam format: one hundred minutes; a score of seven hundred on a scale of one to one thousand passes. Validated against: the official Microsoft S C-two hundred study guide and Microsoft Learn.

1.title: Defender for Office 365: where to investigate
1.text: Defender for Office three sixty-five: where to investigate. The figure shows this: Plan one has real-time detections; Plan two adds Threat Explorer and Take action.

1.title: Defender for Office 365: where to investigate, continued
1.text: Defender for Office three sixty-five: where to investigate. Real-time detections. Plan: Plan one. Notes: Default view Malware; no Go hunt, no U R L clicks view. Threat Explorer. Plan: Plan two. Notes: Default view All email; adds Campaigns, U R L clicks, Go hunt, saved queries. Date filter. Plan: Both. Notes: Default yesterday and today; up to thirty days back; export up to two hundred thousand rows. Plan one adds Safe Attachments, Safe Links, anti-phishing impersonation protection and real-time detections. Plan two adds Threat Explorer, Threat Trackers, Campaigns, attack simulation training, priority account protection and automated investigation and response. Exam tip: Real-time detections equals Plan one. Threat Explorer equals Plan two. If a question needs Campaigns or U R L clicks, the answer is Plan two.

1.title: Take action on email
1.text: Take action on email. In Threat Explorer, select messages and choose Take action. Move or delete: Junk, Inbox, Deleted items, Soft deleted items, Hard deleted items. Plan two. Release quarantined messages. Plan two. Initiate automated investigation. Plan two. Propose remediation (creates a pending soft-delete that another admin approves in the Action center: two-step approval). Plan two. Submit to Microsoft for review; Allow or block entries in the Tenant Allow or Block List. Plan one and two.

1.title: Take action on email, continued
1.text: Take action on email. Soft delete. Moves to Recoverable Items Deletions; the user or admin can recover. Hard delete. Purge; admins can recover only with single item recovery. Roles. Search and Purge to move or delete; Preview to preview or download; Security Reader is read-only. Large selections. Over one hundred entries allow only limited actions.

1.title: Zero-hour auto purge (ZAP)
1.text: Zero-hour auto purge (Z A P). Z A P retroactively acts on messages already delivered when new intelligence marks them bad. It looks at email from the last forty-eight hours in cloud mailboxes. Malware. Quarantined (read or unread). High confidence phishing. Quarantined. Phishing (not high confidence). Follows the anti-spam policy; default Move to Junk; Standard and Strict presets quarantine. Spam. Only unread messages; default Move to Junk. To see Z A P actions: Threat Explorer, then All email, then Additional action equals Z A P. Exam tip: Malware and high-confidence phishing go to quarantine; ordinary spam goes to Junk.

1.title: Microsoft Purview
1.text: Microsoft Purview. If you have Microsoft Purview Insider Risk Management provisioned, its alerts appear in the Defender portal, and you can hunt insider risk events there. Hunting tables Data Security Events and Data Security Behaviors hold user activities that violate Purview policies. Share endpoint alerts with the Microsoft Compliance Center (Module two) so that Purview solutions receive device signals. Response pattern: open the incident, review the user and the activity, then contain the account in Defender or Entra (reset password, revoke sessions, disable) and let the Purview case handle the policy side.

1.title: Defender for Cloud workload protections
1.text: Defender for Cloud workload protections. Prerequisite. Defender for Cloud enabled on the Azure subscription. Access. The unified R back role for Defender for Cloud; without R back you must be Global Administrator or Security Administrator. Informational alerts. Not brought into the Defender portal. Status sync. Defender for Cloud alerts sync both ways; Defender for Endpoint alerts on cloud resources do not sync status. Where you see them. Cloud resources appear in the incident Assets tab and in the attack story. Hunting tables. Cloud Audit Events, Cloud Process Events, Cloud Storage Aggregated Events. Sentinel connector. Use the tenant-based Defender for Cloud (preview) connector; disconnect the legacy subscription-based connector to avoid duplicates. In Defender for Cloud, an alert's Take action tab offers mitigation steps, prevention steps, automated response with a Logic App workflow and suppression.

1.title: Defender for Cloud Apps
1.text: Defender for Cloud Apps. Anomaly detection. Machine learning alerts; tune the sensitivity slider, scope to user groups. oh auth app. Alert on risky or over-privileged apps (for example an app used by more than one hundred users). Activity. Alert on activities such as access from unexpected locations. Session (Conditional Access app control). Monitor or block downloads on unmanaged or risky devices.

1.title: Defender for Cloud Apps, continued
1.text: Defender for Cloud Apps. Suspend user, Require user to sign in again. Contain the account in the app. Confirm user compromised. Sets the user risk to high. Revoke app permissions or Ban app (oh auth). Removes a risky oh auth app. Put in user or admin quarantine, Remove external users, Make private. File actions. Results appear in Cloud Apps, then Governance log. When actions conflict, the stronger action is enforced. File policies retire on January six, twenty twenty-seven; move to Purview D L P or auto-labeling. Exam tip: Compromised oh auth app equals revoke or ban the app. Compromised user equals confirm compromised, suspend or require sign-in again.

1.title: Practice Question 1
1.text: Question one. A phishing campaign delivered the same message to three hundred mailboxes. An analyst with Defender for Office three sixty-five Plan two needs to delete them from the mailboxes. What should be used? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: Threat Explorer, Take action, then Move or delete. Threat Explorer (Plan two) lets you move or delete messages with Take action; the Search and Purge role is needed.

1.title: Practice Question 2
1.text: Question two. A customer has only Defender for Office three sixty-five Plan one. Which view shows recent detections of malware and phishing in near real time? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: Real-time detections, which is available with Plan one. Plan one includes real-time detections; Threat Explorer and Campaigns need Plan two.

1.title: Practice Question 3
1.text: Question three. Zero-hour auto purge finds a delivered message that is now known to be high-confidence phishing. What does Z A P do? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: Moves the message to quarantine. Z A P quarantines malware and high-confidence phishing.

1.title: Practice Question 4
1.text: Question four. An admin soft deletes a malicious message from a mailbox. Where can the item still be recovered from? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: The Recoverable Items Deletions folder. Soft delete moves items to Recoverable Items Deletions; hard delete purges them.

1.title: Practice Question 5
1.text: Question five. An analyst investigates suspicious activity on Kubernetes workloads and wants process-level hunting data from Defender for Cloud. Which table fits? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: Cloud Process Events, the table of cloud process events. Cloud Process Events holds process events for platforms protected by Defender for Containers.

1.title: Practice Question 6
1.text: Question six. A user consented to a risky oh auth app that reads mail. Which Defender for Cloud Apps action removes the threat? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: Revoke the app permissions or ban the app. Revoking oh auth app permissions or banning the app removes the risky app's access.

1.title: Recall Check 1
1.text: Recall check one. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question one. Which plan includes Threat Explorer? Answer: Defender for Office three sixty-five Plan two. Question two. What role is needed to move or delete messages? Answer: Search and Purge. Question three. How far back does Z A P look? Answer: The last forty-eight hours of delivered email.

1.title: Recall Check 2
1.text: Recall check two. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question four. Which governance action sets user risk to high? Answer: Confirm user compromised. Question five. Where is the Defender for Cloud Apps governance log? Answer: Cloud Apps, then Governance log. Question six. When do Cloud Apps file policies retire? Answer: January six, twenty twenty-seven.

1.title: Module Recap
1.text: Here is the recap. Plan one: Real-time detections, Safe Links, Safe Attachments. Plan two: Threat Explorer, Campaigns, U R L clicks, A I R, Take action, attack simulation. Take action: Move or delete, release, investigate, propose remediation; Search and Purge role. Z A P: forty-eight hours; malware and high-confidence phishing to quarantine. Defender for Cloud: tables Cloud Audit Events, Cloud Process Events, Cloud Storage Aggregated Events. Cloud Apps: anomaly, oh auth, activity and session policies; governance log.
